Dave dropped back at the approach to the first hill and Malcolm likewise at the turn into the second; the remaining three staying together until approximately 400 yds…

Beware; Davies, Bhatia and Robinson!! The field events boys were out in force and both Percy Porter and Dave Ansell won their respective events - the hammer, with 158'10½", and the long-jump with a leap of 20'5½".

Normally our middle-distance men could have split forces but on this occasion we had Newell, Robinson, Dabbs and Radford on holiday, Davies injured and Bhatia a 'flu victim; so it was decided to concentrate our remaining forces on the only major road-relay event we tackle before the "Brighton".
Our first team,made up of Shippen, Black, Walker, Robinson, Stearman and Moore wandered between thirteenth and ninth before settling in tenth place- a position far below their capabilities.
On the other hand our runners continue to improve, for in the 2 miles Invitation team race Newell (9-18.4), Dabbs (9-23.8) and Robinson (9-30.2) were only 5 points behind the winners, Polytechnic.
In a tactical half-mile, Robinson and Newell were placed second and third in 1:59.9 and 2:00.2 respectively, and in a similarly run 1500 metres Shipley (second claim) was second in 4:6.2.

He readily agreed to run alternate laps with Dabbs and Robinson, but although winning the race in a new Championship best performance of 29:50.6 he apologised to one of the competitors for not running his laps fast enough!---such is his modesty.

Repetition climbs up the horse-rides in the darkness of Tuesday evenings chasing the unseen figures of Robinson, Miller, Shippen and Thompson; out on the dimly lit roads of Wimbledon on Thursdays, gasping behind Linstead, Dabbs, Gebbett & Co. as they did the "seven hills"; sometimes on the "Warren 9…
After a slow initial couple of circuits the pace was taken up by the Herne Hill pair of Boyle and Robinson who alternated the lead and reeled off laps at about 74 or 75 second pace.

It was Beaglers Mitchinson & Robinson versus Belgravians Nash & Marwood in the steeplechase. Kevin edged closer to Robinson who had set the pace and, still 30 metres down at the bell, closed rapidly round the turn, got to within 10 metres in the back straight, and then flew the final turn with water…

Undoubtedly extremely fit, he was hitting the early part of the stage too hard and by the time the takeover had been reached a posse of five men had jumped him - Scaife (Morpeth), Frank Tickner (a scintillating 17:03 for Wells City), Cox (Bristol), North (Sale) and Robinson (AFD).
Geele, Robinson and Mitchison were all prominent for the Beagles with our own Malachi Byansi, John Kimaiyo and Knut Hegvold also well forward.
